title: Smoothness from Artinian lifting of local stalk homomorphisms
statement: Let $f:Z\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $T$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Fix $z\in Z$, put $t=f(z)$, and let $\varphi=f_z^\sharp:A=\mathcal O_{T,t}\to B=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ be its actual stalk homomorphism. The rings $A,B$ are nonzero Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Local means having a unique maximal ideal, denoted $\mathfrak m_R$ for a local ring $R$, and a local homomorphism has inverse image of the target maximal ideal equal to the source maximal ideal. A small extension is a surjective homomorphism $q:C'\to C$ of nonzero commutative Artinian local rings, meaning that every descending chain of ideals stabilizes, whose kernel is annihilated by $\mathfrak m_{C'}$ and is one-dimensional over $C'/\mathfrak m_{C'}$. Suppose that, for every small extension $q$ and every pair of local homomorphisms $a:A\to C'$ and $b:B\to C$ with $qa=b\varphi$, there is a local homomorphism $c:B\to C'$ satisfying $qc=b$ and $c\varphi=a$. Then there is an open subscheme $U\subseteq Z$ containing $z$ such that $f|_U:U\to T$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Tag 02HX (lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point), implication (3) to (1), expressed using the local rings at the prescribed points rather than scheme test diagrams, together with the Noetherian stalk setup.

proof.text: The stated Noetherian stalk setup follows from the hypotheses. Choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $t$ from the Noetherian affine cover in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. From the affine cover in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose $U=\operatorname{Spec}S\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ containing $z$, with $S$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra. The ring $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. The germ maps identify $A$ and $B$ with localizations of $R$ and $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], so both are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Scheme stalks are local and $\varphi$ is local by [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]; having a maximal ideal makes these rings nonzero.

Use the scheme criterion [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-artinian-lifting-at-point]. Its small extensions are exactly those in the hypothesis: a length-one kernel $I$ is isomorphic to $C'/\mathfrak m_{C'}$, as that statement specifies. Conversely, if $\mathfrak m_{C'}I=0$ and $I$ is one-dimensional over that field, its $C'$-submodules are precisely its vector subspaces, so $0\subsetneq I$ is its only strict submodule chain and its length is one. Every surjection $q:C'\to C$ between the nonzero local rings here is local: the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $C$ is a maximal ideal, hence equals $\mathfrak m_{C'}$. In particular $i=\operatorname{Spec}q$ sends the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ to that of $\operatorname{Spec}C'$, using the inverse-image formula in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization].

source.place: Tag 02HS (definition-small-extension); comparison with the explicit kernel description following that definition.

proof.text: Take arbitrary test data for condition (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-artinian-lifting-at-point]: a small extension $q:C'\to C$, $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}C\to Z$ centred at $z$, and $\beta:\operatorname{Spec}C'\to T$ satisfying $f\alpha=\beta i$. Since $i$ sends closed point to closed point, $\beta$ is centred at $t=f(z)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring], these morphisms give local maps $b:B\to C$ and $a:A\to C'$. Under its germ isomorphisms $\varepsilon_C,\varepsilon_{C'}$, the stalk map of $i$ is $q$: explicitly $i^\sharp\varepsilon_{C'}=\varepsilon_C q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization]. The composition formula [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition] therefore says that the pairs corresponding to $f\alpha$ and $\beta i$ are $(t,b\varphi)$ and $(t,qa)$. Equality of the morphisms gives $qa=b\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 01J6 (lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring), with Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine) for Spec(q); Sheaves Tag 008M (lemma-compose-f-maps-stalks).

proof.text: Apply the assumed local lifting property to these $a,b,q$ to obtain a local $c:B\to C'$ with $qc=b$ and $c\varphi=a$. The bijection [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring] supplies the morphism $\gamma:\operatorname{Spec}C'\to Z$ corresponding to $(z,c)$. The composition formula [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition] identifies $f\gamma$ with the pair $(t,c\varphi)=(t,a)$, hence $f\gamma=\beta$ by injectivity of the bijection. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization], the pair of $\gamma i$ is $(z,qc)=(z,b)$; the same injectivity gives $\gamma i=\alpha$. Thus every test square of step 3 has the required lift, with both equalities for the original scheme morphisms.

We have proved condition (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-artinian-lifting-at-point] at the prescribed point $z$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $f$ is locally of finite type and $T$ locally Noetherian, both given. Its implication (2) to (1) produces an open subscheme containing $z$ on which the original $f:Z\to T$ is smooth. This is the required conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tag 02HX (lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point), (3) implies (1), translating the test squares by Schemes Tag 01J6 and Sheaves Tag 008M.
